processed_notes.note_text: Referred him to Spartanburg Rescue Mission for housing and let him know the intake procedure (walk in at 7am). He called and learned they are full at the moment, so I gave him the phone number for Divinity Care Facility to check if they have openings. Also sent him the application for Soteria.

Session Type: Initial Intake / Consultation

Contact Summary: 
Conducted an initial phone consultation with Terquerious Byrd to assess his current stability, needs, and eligibility for the Turn90 program. Terquerious was recently released from prison (April 30) and is currently on both federal and state probation, wearing an ankle monitor (26 days remaining). His most pressing issue is housing; his current living situation in Spartanburg is highly unstable, and his federal probation officer is considering transferring him back to North Carolina unless he can secure independent housing in SC.

Case Plan Goal Progress: 
- Not yet entered; this was the initial intake assessment.

Briefcase & Gate 1-4 Updates: 
- Identification: Client has physical possession of his Birth Certificate, Social Security Card, and State ID (all issued in North Carolina). 
- Driver's License: Client has never held a driver's license.
- Housing Plan: Urgent barrier. Client needs immediate housing in SC to avoid being transferred to NC.
- Transportation Plan: Major barrier. Client is currently relying on expensive Uber/Lyft rides because public transit does not reach his current location.
- Employment: Client is actively applying for jobs but facing rejections due to his background. Previously attempted to work with Voc Rehab but the compensation ($200/week) was insufficient to survive.

Referrals/Resources Provided: 
- Discussed Turn90's housing partnerships; offered to look into available housing resources in the Spartanburg area to support his desire to stay in SC.
